pfngate release report

A release gate for early-warning models: go or no-go for the stand-in model, with the evidence behind it. Every number comes from a file in results/.

The thresholds are illustrative. They were written after the experiments, for demonstration, in configs/release_criteria.yaml. Out-of-prior performance is reported and is never a pass condition. A criterion that cannot be computed counts as not met. The gate recall rests on very few bad runs.

How big these runs are

  • max_context was reduced from the default 2000 to 200 because the CPU is slow: results/timing_tabpfn.json measured 41 s to predict 200 rows with 2000 context rows.
  • Only the first 3 seeds of each scenario were run (seeds_per_scenario). All scenarios are included, but each has fewer trajectories than the design, so the confidence intervals are wider. This was done after max_context had been reduced, because a full run was still too slow on CPU.

Agent rationale

Recommended alert (confidence 0.850); final decision alert.

The knn context (200 rows, mixed near/far tipping) shows the PFN predicting the query's last window at 0.0047 (essentially at the tipping point) with p_critical of 0.9102. The last third of windows has mean prediction 0.2009 and mean p_critical 0.6327, indicating the system is approaching a tipping point.

5Method and limits

What is simulated

Most of the evidence comes from simulators. In-prior systems are the fold, the subcritical Hopf and the transcritical bifurcation. Out-of-prior systems are rate-induced and noise-induced tipping. Controls are series that never tip, including one that changes regime without tipping. Data are split by system family, never by window. The context pool uses its own seeds, and the gate thresholds were tuned on in-prior validation runs only and frozen before any held-out run.

What is surrogate labelled

The two real datasets are test only. They never enter the context pool and never touch the gate tuning. The Daphnia populations have no known distance to a bifurcation. Their label is a surrogate: how long until extinction, over a fixed horizon, so its scores are not comparable to the simulated ones. The power grid frequency data is normal operation, not a run up to a blackout. Every window is negative, so it can only measure false alarms and has no AUROC.

What the gate cannot know

The gate is plain Python with frozen thresholds. It sees the context and the model output, never the truth. It checks the context size, how far the query is from the pool, how well the context predicts held-out context rows, whether the context holds both near-tipping and far-from-tipping rows, and the integrity of the output. It cannot tell that a series comes from a system unlike anything in the pool when the output still looks plausible. A run is called bad only afterwards, when its prediction interval is compared with the truth. The recall of the gate is measured on few bad runs, so it is uncertain. An LLM agent may recommend but can never override or edit a gate decision.

The model is a stand-in

The model behind every number here is TabPFN, run locally. TipPFN is not public. The backend is swappable, and the TipPFN backend in this repository is a stub that raises an error and documents the input and output it would need. Nothing on this page reproduces TipPFN or says how TipPFN would score.

Size of the runs

These are trial-size runs on a slow CPU: a reduced context and a few seeds per scenario, with a free language model. The intervals are wide. Release criteria are illustrative and were set after the experiments.

Datasets, sources and licences

fingrid_2019-01-01_5d.csv

What
a slice of 5 consecutive days of 1-second grid frequency, 432,000 rows, days 2019-01-01 to 2019-01-05 (naive local time). Used as the split real_control.
Source
Kruse, Schafer and Witthaut, "Pre-Processed Power Grid Frequency Time Series", Zenodo record 3744121, doi:10.5281/zenodo.3744121. File Data_cleansed.zip, member Data_cleansed/Fingrid/2019.zip (Zenodo checksum of the whole zip: md5:cfb08092728bdd0b24b1b71e590c4f3b).
Access date (UTC)
2026-10-31
Licence
CC BY 4.0 (Fingrid, Nordic; pre-processed version released by the record authors). The LICENSE.txt in the same folder of the zip says CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Attribution is required.
Not used
every TransnetBW file (no open licence). None was downloaded.
How fetched
scripts/fetch_grid.py fetch, with HTTP range requests, 3,148,547 bytes read from Zenodo. The slice is the first stretch that is complete and has no large event (every value within 0.25 Hz of 50 Hz, at most 100 NaN seconds a day). The rule is in the script.

daphnia/data-and-code (extinctions.csv, timeseries.csv)

What
weekly census of *Daphnia magna* populations and their extinction dates. Used as the split real_tipping (test only, surrogate labels). See docs/DAPHNIA.md.
Source
Drake and Griffen (2010), "Data from: Early warning signals of extinction in deteriorating environments", Dryad, doi:10.5061/dryad.q3p64 (file data-and-code.zip, Dryad MD5 923e08e6bafae412c43250fef0752ac7). Paper: doi:10.1038/nature09389.
Access date
2026-10-31 (downloaded by hand from Dryad, which needs a login; unzipped into data/raw/daphnia/).
Licence
CC0 1.0 (as given by the Dryad record).
